newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish LOT air cargo may grow 30 pct in 97.
newsitem.headline: Polish LOT air cargo may grow 30 pct in 97.

text.p: Polish airline PLL LOT SA expects air cargo volume to grow 30 percent in 1997 after it jumped 26 percent in January-April against the same period of 1996, a senior LOT official said on Monday.

"The air-cargo season really begins in the second half of the year, so this growth in the first several months is very encouraging and a 30 percent growth is possible," said Iwona Korpalska, deputy-head of LOT's air cargo told Reuters.
LOT transported 22,700 tonnes of air cargo last year, 19 percent more than in 1995 and flew 2.03 million people, up 10.5 percent from 1995.
Korpalska said that during the first four months of the year LOT transported over 6,000 tonnes of cargo.
Korpalska also said that in the first quarter income from air-cargo increased 22 percent against the same period of 1996.

Trade Director Krzysztof Ziebinski earlier on Monday told a news conference that LOT did not plan a near-term purchase of a plane exclusively designed to carry air cargo as the firm concentrated on expanding its fleet of passenger planes.
